props.title: A quick decision guide for the whole stack

left.head: Assemble open-source
rows: Neo4j or RDF + GraphRAG + LangGraph + MCP.
Best for custom or unusual domains.

right.head: Adopt a platform
rows: Palantir Foundry or Azure Digital Twins.
Faster to value, governance built in.
Best when speed beats fine control.

props.foot: Most teams start open-source on one use case, then buy where scale and governance demand it.

props.title: The four failure modes to design against

cards.head: Over-modeling
cards.body: A perfect 500-class ontology no one finishes. Start with 20 that earn their keep.

cards.head: The stale twin
cards.body: Telemetry drifts and the model lies. An out-of-date twin is worse than none.

cards.head: Skipping resolution
cards.body: No entity resolution → duplicate nodes → quietly wrong answers everywhere.

cards.head: Ungoverned agents
cards.body: Untyped actions and no SHACL gate → a confident agent doing real damage.

props.foot: Every one of these is a discipline problem, not a technology problem.

props.title: The numbers that show the map is earning its keep

cards.head: MTTR down
cards.body: Mean time to resolve incidents — the clearest before-and-after number you have.

cards.head: Self-served answers
cards.body: Questions answered by the graph instead of by a senior engineer's DMs.

cards.head: Coverage
cards.body: The share of your systems and sources actually modeled and kept live.

props.foot: Pick one, baseline it before you start, and let the graph earn the next round of investment.

props.title: Three hats — sometimes worn by two people

cards.head: Ontologist / domain expert
cards.body: Owns the shared meaning. Usually a senior engineer who knows the domain — not a PhD in logic.

cards.head: Graph / data engineer
cards.body: Owns construction, entity resolution, validation, and performance — the whole substrate.

cards.head: Agent engineer
cards.body: Owns retrieval, tools, guardrails, and evaluation — the acting mind on top.

props.foot: Add a graph-ML specialist when GNNs enter the picture. You don't need a big team to start.

props.title: The 2026 convergence — and why it matters now

cards.head: Ontology ⨝ Agents
cards.body: Ontology-to-agent pipelines like Neo4j Aura Agent and Palantir + NVIDIA are becoming products.

cards.head: Physical-AI twins
cards.body: Omniverse & OpenUSD extend this exact stack to robots, factories, and cities.

cards.head: Neuro-symbolic default
cards.body: LLM-proposes / graph-verifies is becoming the standard pattern for trustworthy AI.

props.foot: The five topics are collapsing into one discipline — and the teams that see it early win.

props.title: The living map in one breath
props.closer: Give your machines a world — and they'll stop guessing, and start knowing.
items: Ontology = meaning: the shared grammar of entities, relations, and rules.
Knowledge graph = memory: the ontology filled with resolved, real instances.
Digital twin = live senses: the graph synced to reality, able to simulate.
Graph engineering = the body: building, validating, querying, learning at scale.
Agentic engineering = the mind: retrieve, reason, and act — grounded and governed.
Build bottom-up on your own sources; each layer ships value before the next.
